summary: Volume Flow Indicator: signed volume over 130 bars with a volatility cutoff and volume cap, plus a signal line.
overview: The Volume Flow Indicator (VFI), by Markos Katsanos, shows the balance of buying and selling volume in its own pane around zero. It has a signal line in orange and a gradient fill.
Above zero, volume on up moves has been heavier; below zero, on down moves.
how: For each bar, compare typical price with the previous bar. If the change is larger than a cutoff (0.2 x the 30-bar standard deviation of log changes x close), the volume is added as positive or negative. Each bar's volume is capped at 2.5 times average volume.
VFI = sum over 130 bars / average volume, then smoothed with a 3-bar EMA. Signal = 5-bar EMA.
use: Some traders watch VFI above zero as a sign of net buying volume.
Use zero-line crosses as changes in volume flow.
Look for divergence between VFI and price.
Use it on daily charts as in its original design.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
The 130-bar window makes it slow on purpose.
